_note: Original advanced concept questions for hash maps and sets.

questions.title: Membership check
questions.prompt: Which structure best answers “have I seen this value before?”
choices: One boolean for the whole list
questions.explanation: A set stores unique values and gives a direct membership check.

questions.title: Counting characters
questions.prompt: Why is a map useful when checking if two words are anagrams?
choices: It stores a count for each character.
It changes letters into numbers randomly.
questions.explanation: Anagrams need matching counts for each character. A map connects each character to its count.

questions.title: Trace a seen set
questions.code:
seen starts empty
read 3 -> add it
read 1 -> add it
read 3 -> already seen
questions.prompt: Which value is the first repeat?
questions.explanation: The second 3 is the first value that is already in the set.

questions.title: Missing key
questions.prompt: What should code do before increasing a count for a key that may not exist yet?
choices: Change the key to a list.
questions.explanation: A missing key has no count yet, so the safe first value is zero before adding one.

questions.title: Set or map
questions.prompt: You need to know how many times each course code appears. Which structure fits best?
questions.explanation: The course code is the key and the count is the value, so a map fits.

questions.title: Count values
questions.prompt: Arrange the steps to count how many times each value appears.
lines: If the value is missing, start its count at 0.
questions.explanation: A count map starts empty, then each value updates exactly one key.

questions.title: Adding too late
questions.prompt: In a duplicate checker, why should you add a value to `seen` after checking whether it is already there?
choices: So the first copy is not marked as a duplicate.
So every value becomes a duplicate.
questions.explanation: If you add before checking, the current value will always look seen.

questions.title: Keys and values
questions.prompt: In a frequency map for letters, what is the key and what is the value?
questions.explanation: The letter identifies the entry. The count is the information stored for that letter.
